discovery: Conception, design and construction of the ATLAS and CMS detectors, leading to the experimental discovery of the Higgs boson at the LHC
motivation: The 2013 Prize recognised the prediction of the Higgs mechanism, confirmed at CERN's LHC in 2012. The experimental half of this achievement has not yet been honoured. Peter Jenni (founding spokesperson of ATLAS), Michel Della Negra (founding spokesperson of CMS) and Tejinder Virdee (CMS co-founder and architect of its electromagnetic calorimeter) conceived these general-purpose detectors in the late 1980s. They shaped the key design choices, including high-resolution calorimetry and powerful muon systems optimised for H to two photons and H to four leptons, and led them through two decades of construction. That made the discovery possible and opened precision study of the Higgs couplings. The measured Higgs mass shows the electroweak vacuum is near-critical, which changed how our field frames naturalness and the physics beyond the Standard Model. This is a landmark of experimental physics comparable to the W and Z discovery honoured in 1984.
